title: Automated Slide Scanning and Segmentation in Fluorescently-labeled Tissues Using a Widefield High-content Analysis System
protocol: Open the associated software.
Download the journal suite indicated in the Table of Materials.
Import the journal suite to a suitable directory by selecting Import Journal Suite… from the main menu heading Journal.
Select 4X as the magnification, 1 as the camera binning, and 2 as the gain in the Objective and Camera tab.
Input the settings for Plate – Slidescanning under the tab Plate – Slidescanning.
Fill the wells uniformly with sites in the Sites to Visit tab.
Enter the values displayed in Figure 1B by clicking on Edit Plate Bottom Settings….
Enter the desired wavelength for the preview scan under the Acquisition Loop tab.
Enable Shading Correction in Plate Acquisition mode to stitch images together.
Save these settings as Setting A.

Select 40X as the magnification, 1 as the camera binning (for the highest digital resolution), and 2 as the gain (to increase the signal and brightness of images) for Slide Acquisition at High Magnification.
Ensure all settings for the Plate – Slidescanning and Edit Plate Bottom Settings… tabs are the same as that for Setting A.
If the images obtained are not crisp, change the Well depth, Plate height, and Plate Bottom Settings to adjust the focus.
Choose Laser with Image Recovery under the Autofocus options section if there is still an issue with the focus.
Enter the number of wavelengths present in the sample.
Check the Enable laser-based focusing option.
Check the Enable image-based focusing for acquisition or laser recovery option.
Select Focus on plate and well bottom under Autofocus tab.
Select the options as indicated in Figure 2 under Journals tab.
Ensure Prevent asynchronous hardware moves is selected.
Save settings as Setting B.
Press F4 to get the Main Menu.
Select Slide Scanning.
Click Open Door – Eject Slide.
Insert slide(s) and the slide adapter into the WHCAS with coverslip facing down and label on the side of the notch.
Close Door – Load Slide.
Under Screening heading, select Plate Acquisition and Control… and Plate Acquisition Setup… and load Setting A.
Move to the well containing the sample under Wells to Visit tab.
Move to different sites with Live image capture until cells are located under Sites to Visit tab.
Manually focus on the sample or use Autofocus.
Use Snap to capture the image.
On the main menu, select Preview Slides.
Select the option reflecting how many slides are going to be scanned in the dialog box that appears.
Scan one slide at a time and press OK.
Select 4X as the magnification.
Press OK.
Select Coverslip down (0.17 mm) as the slide orientation.
Use a correction collar if a different coverslip thickness is used.
Press OK.
Click Continue.
Under Load Scan Slide Setting, ensure the Acquisition settings and Calibrations boxes are checked.
Press Cancel.
When the Scan Slide Settings box reappears, select Continue.
Adjust the settings in the Scan Slide dialog box as suggested.
Select Close when finished.
Select a directory for the slide scanning data.
Click OK.
Enter a name for the file.
Click OK.
Use the Rectangular Region tool to select the entire preview scan region.
Click Continue.
The preview slide scan will now commence.
When the preview is completed, continue.
Load the setup for high magnification scanning.
Determine which wells are to be imaged under the Wells to Visit tab.
Move to the well containing the sample using the right-click button on the mouse.
Locate different sites with the Live feature until the cells or tissue is found.
Manually focus on the sample or use Autofocus.
Capture the image using Snap.
Adjust Step size in Plate Acquisition and Control dialog box if necessary.
Ensure the DAPI Scan selects the low-magnification slide image properly.
Press OK to select the DAPI Scan.
Highlight the Plate Acquisition Snap - DAPI when asked for the plate acquisition snap.
Click on OK.
Use the Rectangular Region tool to select regions of interest on the DAPI Scan.
Press Continue when the Create or Load Regions box appears.
Select No under the Load Regions dialog box.
Highlight the largest region of interest using the Locator tool.
Press Continue under the Select Region dialog box.
Select Continue when the Confirm regions box appears.
Choose whether the region needs to be saved in the Save Regions dialog box.
Choose Tiled or 10% overlap in the Site Spacing dialog box and click OK.
Dismiss the Setup Complete box by pressing Continue.
Keep the Acquisition Site Setup for 40X box open.
Enter columns and rows into the Plate Acquisition Setup box based on the information from the Acquisition Site Setup for 40X box.
Keep the WellPositions box open in the bottom left-hand corner.
Highlight the same number of wells as regions of interest previously selected in the Wells to Visit box.
Enter the suggested columns and rows under the Sites to Visit tab.
Click on Tile sites after entering the columns and rows.
Press Acquire Plate under the Summary tab to position the stage at a pre-selected region of interest.
Once the camera pans over a site containing cells, press Cancel to stop image acquisition.
Ensure the stage is now located over the sample.
Optimize wavelength settings to obtain a focused and high dynamic range image.
Click on the Summary tab when satisfied with the settings.
Acquire Plate after optimizing the settings.
Select the desired custom module for image analysis.
Run the analysis on all sites.
Exclude any sites with poor image quality.
Select the region of interest within the tumor sample's edges.
Exclude out-of-focus sites.
Exclude sites containing tissue folds or tears.
Use the Laser focus score as a threshold to exclude low-quality sites.
Exclude large blood vessels and areas of necrosis if necessary.
Include only hypercellular areas of interest if required.
